transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start: 10:00 UTC
Duration: 72 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Lee, Ava Chen, Diego Ramirez, Priya Nair, Samir Patel, Helen Zhou, Lina Park, Jorge Alvarez, Sam (QA)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Discussed KV eviction thresholds causing noisy OOM-like behavior under bursty mixed seq lengths.
- Looked at early smoothing prototype that ramps concurrency per-worker to reduce tail spikes.
- Agreed to run more realistic sims, add telemetry, and prepare canary with rollback gates.

Topics covered: KV eviction, concurrency smoothing, autoscaler interactions, telemetry, canary plan, incident rehearsal

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Marcus: alright um hey everyone thanks for joining, let's kick off, objective for today is to lock down the eviction and smoothing plan so we can test a canary, priya you ok with the agenda?
[00:23] Priya: yep that's the plan, want to make sure we have acceptance criteria—like percent tail-latency budget we can tolerate and no regression in P50 cost, yeah.
[00:36] Ava: real quick, ops background: oncall saw two incidents this month where KV thrash precipitated long tails, looked like eviction churn when a spike of short-seq requests hit a worker that had big-seq KV in memory.
[00:55] Diego: right, that's the core problem. Current LRU-ish heuristic evicts based on last access, but we don't consider sequence-length affinity — long-seq KV are expensive to recompute and we should bias to keep them if the worker tends to get long sequences.
[01:14] Jorge: (cuts in) is that the thing you called KV hot-set? I might, um, have mis-said earlier, but it seems like we lose warm KVs too frequently.
[01:26] Diego: yeah hot-set by seq length and model shard. The eviction cost delta is huge for 32k-context variants.
[01:38] Samir: one caveat is memory fragmentation on GPUs, sometimes pages can't be reclaimed, so even a perfect heuristic won't fully avoid OOMs, but it reduces tail events.
[01:50] Marcus: good, so two parallel work streams: improve eviction heuristic + smoothing layer that controls per-worker concurrency ramping. Diego you own eviction sim, Ava owns the rollout ops plan, samir you'll validate infra interaction?
[02:06] Samir: yep, I can run tests with the autoscaler toggled and check for oscillation with smoothing enabled.
[02:15] Helen: telemetry note — current dashboards don't show per-route KV hit rate, we just have aggregate. We need per-model, per-route KV hit rate, and a per-worker tail-latency heatmap.
[02:30] Marcus: agreed. Helen can you add those panels?
[02:34] Helen: I'll add basic panels, but need names of key routes and the label we use for seq-length buckets.
[02:42] Priya: I'll produce a list of top 10 routes by traffic and example seq-length distribution.
[02:48] Diego: about the sim: initial runs used synthetic homogeneous load, which hid the mixed seq behavior. I'm going to run mixed seq-length traces based on prod-sampled traces for a full day. Expect results in about a week.
[03:05] Marcus: timeline seems fine. What's the smoothing prototype looking like now? Diego?
[03:12] Diego: prototype is simple: per-worker token-smoothing window that caps concurrency growth based on recent tail-latency percentiles. We slowly increase concurrency target over N seconds instead of ramping immediately. Works in bench but hasn't been tested against autoscaler, also need to ensure it doesn't amplify latency for low-load customers.
[03:34] Ava: that slow ramp is good for graceful handling, but from ops I want emergency bypass: if queue depth exceeds X or if memory pressure is high we drop smoothing and trigger fallback path to lower-cost model or reduce request size.
[03:49] Marcus: ok so bypass gates: memory pressure and queue depth; add SLO-based gate.
[03:55] Jorge: question — do we plan to apply smoothing at the routing layer or within the worker runtime? Implications for observability.
[04:05] Diego: in runtime. Routing layer would be coarser; runtime gives per-worker state. But runtime change is riskier on canary.
[04:15] Priya: product preference is runtime if it's invisible to customers, but we need a fallback to a routing-level mitigation if runtime fails.
[04:26] Sam (QA): how do we validate in staging? We can replay prod traces but we need to preserve timing. I'm worried about nondeterministic timing in bench infra.
[04:38] Diego: agreed, part of sim work is to create a trace-replayer that preserves inter-arrival distributions. I'll do that.
[04:45] Marcus: good. Helen, what telemetry do we need for canary acceptance?
[04:49] Helen: kv hit-rate per-model, tail P95/P99 latency per-worker and per-route, queue depth, memory pressure, and autoscaler scale events. Also percent of requests that hit smoothing gate.
[05:05] Ava: and alerting rules: P99 > baseline + 25% for more than 5 minutes should roll back automatically. Also need a manual rollback button in the console.
[05:18] Marcus: noted. Let's talk numbers: what tail-latency delta are we willing to accept? Priya?
[05:25] Priya: product requirement: no more than 10% increase in P99 for high-tier customers, and overall we target a 15% reduction in burst-driven OOM events. If smoothing reduces OOMs but P99 regresses >10% for top routes we don't proceed.
[05:42] Diego: in bench runs smoothing reduced spike P99 by ~30% but increased steady-state P99 by ~6% in some cases due to slower concurrency fill. That seems within product bands.
[05:56] Marcus: good. Competitors: quick note — Anthropic paper used a similar smoothing idea on their serving layer, but they applied it at the routing level. We should call out differences.
[06:10] Jorge: will canary be per-region? I think APAC has different seq distribution.
[06:17] Marcus: we'll canary regionally: start in us-west with 10% of traffic, monitor 48h, ramp to 25% over 48h if metrics good. Avoid APAC initial canary.
[06:29] Samir: autoscaler test plan — smoothing reduces instantaneous CPU/token concurrency which may cause autoscaler to think load is lower and scale down; need to ensure it doesn't scale down under-smoothing. I'll test with autoscaler aggressiveness +/-2.
[06:44] Diego: also eviction heuristics have tune knobs: evict-by-cost, evict-by-last-access, and preserve-by-model-shard. We'll add a weight function and run grid search in sim.
[06:56] Marcus: can you sketch acceptance criteria for the eviction change?
[07:01] Diego: eviction change acceptance: no increase in OOM events in sim, KV recompute cost across cluster should reduce by >20% for long-seq heavy routes, and overall token cost delta within +/-3%.
[07:16] Priya: product wants a regression test that runs nightly in CI for the eviction changes with a minimized trace to catch regressions.
[07:25] Sam (QA): we'll add that. Diego, we'll need a test harness that integrates with CI.
[07:30] Diego: yep I'll publish a containerized harness.
[07:34] Helen: observability follow-up — I'll tag telemetry with canary_id and smoothing_flag to make rollback comparisons trivial.
[07:45] Marcus: nice. Let's discuss incident rehearsals. Ava?
[07:49] Ava: we'll run a tabletop on the week of canary with Oncall and Support. Playbook steps: detect via alert, pause canary traffic, enable rollback, escalate to eng if rollback fails. We should rehearse rollback twice.
[08:03] Marcus: schedule it. Also need a small runbook doc for PM and CS to set expectations. Priya you will draft it.
[08:12] Priya: on it.
[08:16] Diego: one more tech nuance — when evicting, we should consider async prefetch: when a long-seq request arrives and key isn't present, issue background prefetch for next tokens. That reduces tail if prefetch succeeds. But it increases memory churn. Need to weigh.
[08:33] Samir: prefetch might interact badly with multi-tenant sharing. Maybe restrict prefetch to dedicated pools.
[08:41] Marcus: ok mark prefetch as experiment only for dedicated pools.
[08:46] Jorge: are there cost implications for preserving KV? More memory = more infra cost. Priya? product impact?
[08:54] Priya: product is ok with slight cost increase if tail-latency and OOMs drop. We'll quantify in acceptance criteria.
[09:03] Sam (QA): question — what about quantized models? Eviction cost for a quantized model vs full precision differs, does our heuristic account for model format?
[09:13] Diego: not yet, sim will include quantized variants. We'll add model-format weight.
[09:20] Marcus: good. Let's capture who's doing what. Diego: eviction sim and harness, include quantized + mixed seq. Diego due 2026-10-07.
[09:29] Marcus: Helen: telemetry panels and canary tagging, due 2026-10-05.
[09:34] Marcus: Samir: autoscaler interaction tests, due 2026-10-08.
[09:39] Marcus: Ava: ops playbook + tabletop scheduling, due 2026-10-04.
[09:44] Marcus: Priya: product doc + routes list, due 2026-10-06.
[09:49] Priya: I'll also prepare the acceptance criteria doc.
[09:54] Diego: quick note on rollback — we need to ensure model-variant fallback is fast, that means pre-warming the fallback variant. That costs. Ops needs to decide pre-warm windows.
[10:04] Ava: prefer on-demand pre-warm then hold for short time if traffic persists, avoid constant pre-warm costs. We'll test heuristics.
[10:12] Marcus: final section: risk register quick hit. Major risks: evict heuristic mis-tune -> regression in P99, smoothing interacts with autoscaler -> under-provisioning, prefetch amplifies memory churn. Mitigations assigned.
[10:26] Marcus: wrap up — next meeting in two weeks unless blockers. We'll reconvene after Diego's sim results.
[10:34] Priya: can we have a quick sync after telemetry panels are live to finalize canary gating?
[10:39] Helen: yes, ping me and I'll stand up a short meeting.
[10:43] Marcus: great, thanks everyone. End meeting.

--- End transcript ---
